title: Other Dominical Sayings Cited by Paul (1 Cor 7:10–11; 9:14; 1 Thess 4:15–17)
source_edition: Westcott-Hort 1881 (byztxt/greektext-westcott-hort, Sandborg-Petersen ed.); rendered in canon-style unaccented form.
convention_notes: Text presented without diacritical marks; canon-style unaccented form; final sigma rendered as σ (medial form); medial mu rendered as µ.
date_of_composition: 1 Corinthians c. 53–55 CE; 1 Thessalonians c. 50–51 CE — the earliest extant Christian writing.
scope_note: Three Pauline citations of dominical command beyond the eucharistic and resurrection-appearance traditions. The divorce saying (1 Cor 7:10–11) is among the most multiply-attested Jesus traditions, paralleled in Mark 10:11–12 and Q (Lk 16:18 // Mt 5:31–32). The support-for-proclaimers command (1 Cor 9:14) parallels Q (Lk 10:7 // Mt 10:7–10) and is cited explicitly as scripture at 1 Tim 5:18. The parousia saying (1 Thess 4:15–17), introduced as 'in a word of [the] Kyrios' (en logō kyrioy) using LXX prophetic-formula vocabulary, is the earliest extant Christian eschatological text and has no exact synoptic parallel.
